<thought>Based on the observed mass spectrum, the isotopic envelope shows a dominant monoisotopic peak at m/z 179 with progressively smaller peaks at +1, +2, +3 Da, etc. The relative intensities do not match the characteristic patterns of chlorine (M+2 ≈ 30 % of M) or bromine (M+2 ≈ 100 % of M). The M+2 peak is only about 1 % of the base peak, which is far lower than the ~4 % expected for a single sulfur atom (34S) and could be explained by contributions from multiple C‑13 atoms rather than sulfur. Consequently, no element exhibits a distinctive isotopic signature that can be unambiguously identified from this spectrum alone. Therefore, the list of definitively identifiable elements is empty.>
